metadata.note: The Hampton and Branchville Railroad and Lumber Company (chartered 16 Dec 1891; renamed Hampton and Branchville Railroad 1924, a name change only) never reached Branchville. It ran NE from Hampton (Charleston & Western Carolina connection) through Crocketville, Miley, Moselle and Ashton to H&B Junction on the ACL Walterboro Branch (16 mi, open by 1 Jan 1901), then on to Padgett and Smoaks (Feb 1909) and Cannadys (by 1933). Passenger service is confirmed from the 1902 Official Guide to the December 1951 Guide (one daily-except-Sunday train Hampton - Cannadys); neither end is a known opening or closing, so every span is drawn [OPEN]. Drawn: Hampton - H&B Junction 1902-1951, H&B Junction - Smoaks 1926-1951, Smoaks - Cannadys 1933-1951, and the H&B's 1905 run over the ACL from H&B Junction to Lodge as a one-year [ANCHOR]. One operating company throughout (control passed from the Mauldin heirs to the Lightsey family without changing who ran the trains), so no Rule 4 split.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue, Hampton & Branchville Railroad entry dated December 1951 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt, line ~112650)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py (degree-tile rail graph + per-railroad cache). The road's own line is OSM railway=rail named 'Hampton and Branchville' (no old_railway_operator tag); the lifted Smoaks/Cannadys extension and the ACL Lodge stretch are OSM railway=abandoned ways. OpenHistoricalMap returned nothing for the road. Waypoint geocodes (Nominatim) were type-checked: Padgett (-> Padgett Acres, Columbia), Hiott(s) (-> a cemetery) and Bennetts (-> Bennetts Point) were wrong places and were not used; Hampton and H&B Junction were hand-pinned.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] ends on every drawn span: passenger START is confirmed only from 1902 (Hampton - H&B Junction), 1926 (to Smoaks) and 1933 (to Cannadys) - the first Guide listings in Fowler - though the lines opened 1892-1901, 1909 and 1926-33; passenger END is confirmed only to Dec 1951 (Feb 1952 Guide) on all three, with no last-train date found (Palmetto Railways: 'until about the 1950s'). Chronicling America pages for 1895-1924 (Savannah Morning News 1896-10-09 p6, 1898-09-15 p3; Manning Times 1904-03-30 p1) and the Hampton County Guardian are the places to look. (2) [ANCHOR] H&B Junction - Lodge over the ACL drawn for 1905 only. (3) Whether the 1951 train was mixed; the 'Boll Weevil' car nickname. (4) Mauldinton (1902 terminus) location - if beyond the junction, part of the Smoaks extension carried passengers by 1902. (5) Smoaks - Cannadys construction date. (6) Positions of Hiotts, Bennetts and Sidney: the report lists Sidney between Smoaks and Cannadys, but Nominatim puts Sidney, Colleton County, at (-80.568, 33.000), SE of Canadys on the grade toward Cottageville - unresolved. (7) ICC 16 mi vs Guide 17 mi to H&B Junction. All headways and speeds are estimates (only the 1951 schedule is sourced). (8) Exact divergence of the Smoaks extension at H&B Junction (drawn as a 0.84 mi straight line).
metadata.omitted: Cannadys - Cottageville (12 mi): Dec 1951 Guide 'No regular service between Cannadys and Cottageville'; Fowler 'irregular service only beyond Cannadys, passengers?'. No confirmable passenger year - not drawn (report block [5], drawable NONE).
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Mauldin and Sons lumber tram (1890, ~6 mi E of Hampton; logging only). All post-passenger freight operation: the Canadys power-plant coal traffic (to Dec 2012) over the 1962 ACL Stokes - Canadys spur and the ex-ACL Walterboro - Stokes trackage the H&B bought from CSX (1986 or 1988 - sources conflict), and the 2026 Palmetto Railways Salkehatchie Subdivision reactivation. None ever carried passengers; none drawn (Rule 1).

segments.note: [OPEN] both ends. Hampton (connection with the Charleston & Western Carolina) - Crocketville - Miley - Moselle - Ashton - Hampton & Branchville Junction (formerly Mauldins Junction; crossing/connection with the ACL Walterboro Branch). The Hampton and Branchville Railroad and Lumber Company (chartered 1891, renamed Hampton and Branchville Railroad 1924 - a name change, same operating company) had the line open to the junction by 1 Jan 1901 (ICC valuation) and was a freight common carrier from Sept 1892 (Palmetto Railways). START 1902 [OPEN]: the first POSITIVE passenger evidence is the 1902 Official Guide (Fowler lists Mauldinton as terminus of service in 1902G; its location is uncertain, but it can only be reached over this line). 1902 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known opening - passenger service may have begun anywhere from 1892 to 1902; do not extend earlier without evidence. 1902-1925 the trains ended at or near the junction (in 1905 they ran on to Lodge over the ACL - separate [ANCHOR] feature); from 1926 they ran through to Smoaks and from 1933 to Cannadys (separate features). END 1951 [OPEN]: passenger service is confirmed to December 1951 by the Feb 1952 Official Guide (one train daily except Sunday, Hampton 9:45 a.m. - H&B Junction - Cannadys 12:00 noon, returning Cannadys 1:30 p.m. - Hampton 3:40 p.m.; all stations indexed without the freight-only dagger). This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped (Palmetto Railways says only 'until about the 1950s'). Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE: the Dec 1951 Guide shows one daily-except-Sunday round trip; no earlier frequency is sourced, and whether the train was mixed is not established. Freight continued after passengers ended (coal to the Canadys power plant until Dec 2012; Palmetto Railways' Salkehatchie Subdivision reactivation, 2026) - freight only, not drawn (Rule 1).
sources: Segment-level: start 1902 from Fowler, South Carolina railroads file table 76 (Mauldinton '1902G'); route and the 1 Jan 1901 opening from the ICC valuation abstract; end 1951 and the 1951 service from the Feb 1952 Official Guide H&B entry (Dec 1951) and its station index - all as read in research/branches/hampton_and_branchville_railroad.txt (2026-11-05); the tracer did not re-open these sources. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: [OPEN] both ends. H&B Junction - Padgett - (Strickland Switch / Mauldinton?) - Smoaks. The 1951 train ran through to Cannadys, which can only be reached via Smoaks. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE: the Dec 1951 Guide shows one daily-except-Sunday round trip; no earlier frequency is sourced, and whether the train was mixed is not established. Freight continued after passengers ended (coal to the Canadys power plant until Dec 2012; Palmetto Railways' Salkehatchie Subdivision reactivation, 2026) - freight only, not drawn (Rule 1).

No approximated (straight-line) legs beyond a 71 m join across the junction. ANOTHER COMPANY'S TRACK: this whole feature is drawn on the Atlantic Coast Line's Walterboro Branch, not on H&B-owned track - it records H&B trains running over the ACL in 1905, and is coloured and labelled for the H&B because the H&B ran the trains. No ACL Walterboro Branch feature exists in data/. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on OSM's abandoned-railway trace of the ACL branch; no historical map was checked against it.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Single proven year. Fowler's H&B table header notes that 'in 1905G, service continued over BEW (25) to Lodge' - i.e. in the 1905 Official Guide H&B trains ran on from H&B Junction over the Atlantic Coast Line Walterboro Branch to the ACL station at Lodge (ACL table 25: H&B Junction mi 32.0, Lodge 33.3), presumably for connections, before the 1909 Smoaks extension. Service certainly ran wider than 1905 in both directions but no other year is confirmed: do NOT widen this anchor without a dated timetable. The track is the ACL's; this feature records H&B trains on it, not the ACL's own service. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE: the Dec 1951 Guide shows one daily-except-Sunday round trip; no earlier frequency is sourced, and whether the train was mixed is not established.
